title: A resignation (2013)
hook: Benedict XVI announces, in Latin, that he will step down as pope

segments.voice: Yesterday, Benedict the Sixteenth and his first letter, Deus caritas est. Your line was God is love.

It's a routine morning meeting in the Vatican, the kind where cardinals gather to approve dates for new saints. The business is done. Then the pope picks up a sheet of paper and begins to read, in Latin. Not everyone in the room follows the Latin at speed. Those who do go very still. He has examined his conscience before God, again and again, he says, and his strength, with advancing age, is no longer enough for the work. And so he is renouncing the ministry of the bishop of Rome. On a set evening, at a set hour, the see of Peter will be empty. Then he puts the paper down.
screen: `A ROUTINE MEETING, IN LATIN.` → `MY STRENGTH IS NO LONGER ENOUGH.` → `THE SEE OF PETER WILL BE EMPTY.`

segments.voice: That morning raises four questions. First, was it allowed? Yes. People were stunned, but nothing in it broke the Church's law, which has a short line for this: a pope may renounce his office, provided he does it freely and makes it properly known, and it needs nobody's acceptance. Second, the reason he gave. No scandal, no pressure. He named his own body and mind: the work of a pope, in a fast-changing world, needs vigor of both, and in him that vigor had declined. He didn't dress it up. Third, what came after. He didn't go far. He moved into a small monastery inside the Vatican gardens, wore white, called himself pope emeritus, and said he would serve the Church hidden from the world, by prayer. Some theologians and canon lawyers have questioned parts of that arrangement, the title and the white, and they still discuss what a retired pope should be. Fourth, what it says. Ecclesiastes, in the Douay-Rheims, begins a poem: "All things have their season." A few lines on: "a time to keep, and a time to cast away." Catholics read Benedict's choice in more than one way. Some saw courage and humility, a man putting the work above his own place in it. Some were unsettled, and wondered what it would mean for the papacy after him. Either way, he did a hard thing plainly: he said, I can't do this well anymore, and he stepped down.
screen: `THE CHURCH'S LAW ALLOWS IT.` · `HONEST ABOUT BODY AND MIND.` · `A MONASTERY IN THE GARDENS.` · `ALL THINGS HAVE THEIR SEASON.` · then, large: `HE STEPPED DOWN.`

segments.voice: Is there something you hold on to because letting go would look like failure: a role, a commitment, a habit, a grudge, a title? Not everything should be dropped; just ask Benedict's question, can I still do this well, and answer as plainly as he did, without excuses or drama. If you pray, bring the answer to God; if not, let it be true for a minute.
A resignation. Benedict the Sixteenth's renunciation, read in Latin to a gathering of cardinals, because his strength was no longer enough for the work.
Your line: he stepped down. A season ended, and he said so plainly. Until next time.

howItsDone: When a pope dies or resigns, the see of Rome is vacant until the cardinals meet in conclave to elect a successor; Catholics pray for the Church and for the cardinals during that time.

notes: Claims rule: the outline hook's 'first pope to resign in about six hundred years' is a superlative and number not in a cited text, so it is not stated.

Declaratio: confirm the consistory setting (approval of canonizations), 'examined my conscience before God', 'ingravescente aetate', vigor of mind and body, and the set hour of vacancy. Original-language phrase should be checked against the Latin text.
Canon 332 §2: confirm the paraphrase (freely made, properly manifested, not needing acceptance).
Mater Ecclesiae monastery, the title 'pope emeritus', the white cassock, and 'hidden from the world' (from his last general audience / farewell): confirm.
'Some theologians and canon lawyers have questioned parts of that arrangement' is a general claim without a cited text; Keeper may cut.
Ecclesiastes 3:1 Douay-Rheims: confirm 'All things have their season'.
